title: Resonance detection and suppression tests
description:
Add juce::UnitTest coverage for SpectralAnalysisEngine, ResonanceDetector, and ResonanceSuppressor per SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §8 and §21.6.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/Analysis/SpectralAnalysisEngine.* and AnalysisFifo.* public APIs from g.1
- Source/DSP/ResonanceDetector.* candidate/persistence APIs from g.2
- Source/DSP/ResonanceSuppressor.* slot/process/audition APIs from g.3
- Source/DSP/PitchDetector.* f0 snapshot API (for harmonic-rejection cases)
- tests/TestMain.cpp and existing tests/*Tests.cpp patterns (phases B–F)
- CMakeLists.txt as left by g.3 (tests/ResonanceTests.cpp should already be listed — do not edit CMake unless the entry is missing)
- .abracapocus/SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §8.2–8.7 and §21.6 (fixed sine resonances, moving harmonics, pink-noise peaks, scan does not auto-modify sound)

Implement tests/ResonanceTests.cpp:
1. SpectralAnalysisEngine/AnalysisFifo: push a steady sine (e.g. 1 kHz) through prepare + enough frames; latest spectrum shows a clear peak near the expected bin within documented tolerance; drop/skip-frame counters remain finite; disabled engine stops advancing expensive work (or at least remains safe to call).
2. ResonanceDetector + fixed narrow excess: inject/synthesize spectrum or audio with a fixed high-Q tone (e.g. ~4.2–4.35 kHz) over noise → candidate list contains a near-frequency high-confidence persistent peak after persistence builds.
3. Harmonic rejection: with PitchDetector.f0 (or injected f0) set so a peak sits on m*f0 and tracks note changes, candidate confidence is lower than an equal-level fixed off-harmonic peak present across different f0 values (assert ordering or threshold relationship, not sample-identical audio).
4. Scan workflow: beginScan/endScan (or equivalent) produces bounded cards; detector/suppressor path does not alter process() output until applyCandidate/explicit enable on a slot (bit-identical or near-identical dry vs unapplied path within float tolerance).
5. ResonanceSuppressor: enabling a static notch at a known sine frequency reduces output energy at that frequency vs bypass; depth/Q clamps respect 0–18 dB and Q 3–40 bounds; removed-signal audition energy is elevated when notch is deep (optional if API exposes wet/removed buffers).
6. Six slots constructible/settable; out-of-range frequency/Q/depth inputs clamp safely to finite coefficients.
7. Use juce::UnitTest; no new third-party test frameworks. Do not rewrite production DSP solely to force green tests — only assert documented tolerances.
